title: Bitcoin edges lower as rate risks persist, regulated derivatives expand and portfolio value rises
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $63,700, down 0.6% over 24 hours, while ether edged up 0.3% to about $1,802. The broader crypto market fell 3.0% to roughly $2.17 trillion. Ether's small recovery therefore sits within a weaker overall market. Higher borrowing costs remain a relevant risk for speculative assets, with the newly released Federal Reserve minutes reinforcing the prospect of further tightening.

The Fed minutes showed that almost all participants considered additional rate increases likely to be appropriate under their economic outlooks. The committee had held its target range at 3.75% to 4%, with two members preferring a quarter-point increase. A couple of participants said a larger increase could merit consideration if inflation data disappointed. For crypto, the implication is continued competition from interest-bearing assets and more expensive leverage. The minutes explain the policy backdrop without establishing the cause of every price move.

Backpack announced approval to operate as a Futures Commission Merchant, adding the customer-facing intermediary license to its exchange and clearinghouse approvals. The company says the completed framework will let U.S. customers access leveraged perpetual futures and event contracts, with fiat and crypto collateral and a unified global order book. This creates another regulated route into products often associated with offshore venues. The announcement describes planned access; the licenses themselves do not establish how much customer activity the platform will attract.

Hyundai Card and JPMorgan's Kinexys reported a treasury-management proof of concept in which AI agents detected a euro liquidity shortfall, requested foreign-exchange quotes and booked a simulated conversion. The test used signed mandates, identity checks, transaction controls and an audit trail, with options for human review or rejection. No live money moved. Its significance is practical: it tests how institutions could delegate narrowly defined financial tasks to software while preserving authority limits and records, rather than assuming that an agent's request is sufficient authorization.

Our on-chain portfolio is worth about $57,000, comprising $9,419 in the active treasury and $47,625 in the Safe. The marked value rose $342, or 0.6%, from the previous comparable snapshot. Direct ARC balances are worth about $39,400, or 69% of the total, alongside $5,575 in the Safe's WETH/ARC pool. ARC remains the dominant concentration. The treasury's ARC balance increased by about 12,213 tokens to 248,627. Beefy positions total $1,791 across several pools, and Curve holds $428 in a basket of Brazilian-real tokens.

Aave collateral across both wallets totals about $6,163 in WETH against $3,150 of USDC debt. The treasury health factor is unchanged at 1.87; the Safe improved slightly from 1.49 to 1.50. Fluid's collateral mix shifted toward USDC and away from syrupUSDC, but its roughly $1,220 of collateral still supports $1,066 of debt. Its $154 net position remains small, with a 1.03 health factor leaving very limited liquidation headroom.

sources.title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, October 27–28, 2026
Backpack Secures Futures Commission Merchant License and NFA Membership, Completing U.S. CFTC Regulatory Framework
Hyundai Card and Kinexys by J.P. Morgan advance trust framework for safe AI-agent transactions
